newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares limp higher, seen dragging feet.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares limp higher, seen dragging feet.

text.p: Slovenian shares firmed a touch on Thursday and traders said they expect the market to show little movement until a new prime minister is named, probably in the second half of December.
"The market will be uneasy until it is clear who will form the new government," one trader said.
He said shares could start rising once a prime minister is named -- regardless of who it turns out to be.

Although the Liberal Democrats of current Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek were the strongest single party in the November general election, winning 25 out of 90 parliamentary seats, they are facing a loose alliance of rightist "Spring" parties, who got 45 seats.
The alliance, comprising the People's Party, Social Democrats and Christian Democrats, is pushing for Marjan Podobnik, head of the People's Party, to be prime minister.

"Podobnik did not seem to be in favour of the European Union prior to elections but he seems to be softening now. Therefore little change in the policy towards EU can be expected no matter who leads the new government," Karmen Korbun, a broker of bank Creditanstalt said.

She said, however, prices could jump before the end of December, regardless of whether the political situation clears up by then, due to a new 25-percent tax on profits individuals make with securities that will be enforced from January.
"Brokerages may decide to buy at higher prices at the end of the year in order to reduce future profits and thus lower tax that will have to be paid next year," Korbun said.
The 10-share SBI index firmed 3.84 points to 1,145.5.
Overall eight shares rose, six fall, three were unchanged and eight were untraded.
Turnover fell to 70.9 million tolars from 269.9 million.
Port Luka Koper had the biggest turnover, rising 1.77 percent to 2,188 tolars on volume of 8,646 shares for total turnover of 18.8 million tolars.
Brokerage Nika was the top gainer, rising 2.38 percent to 4,044 on volume of 616 shares for total turnover of 2.5 million tolars.

Financial consultancy Finmedia was the leading decliner, closing 8.57 percent lower at 14,620 on volume of 99 shares for total turnover of 1.5 million tolars. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana Newsroom, 386 61 1263 644
